The new rising main enables wastewater to be fed to the WWTP at a higher flow rate than previously occurred, causing the splitter box to overflow. The level sensor in the splitter box shows the level significantly increased prior to the puddles being observed, however, there is no high level switch within the splitter box that gives data on when the splitter box is overflowing (the level sensor's maximum level is lower than the overflow point).

At 14:45 noticed a VEOLIA Liquid Waste truck using the Septic Receival bay at Heathfield WWTP. At 15:45 noticed the VEOLIA Liquid Waste truck pulling out of bay & I thought to myself "he took longer than usual". A different company truck pulled in straight after to use the facilities & I noticed that he was having a problem with the hose for discharging. I walked up to see what the issue was & noticed that the hose & the pipework/valves for receiving were blocked up with sand. The VEOLIA truck was parked 20 meters up from the plant on the side of the road. I decided to speak to the driver about the issue that has been caused. Upon arriving on the drivers side of the VEOLIA truck, saw that the driver was on the phone so I patiently waited for him to finish his conversation & wind the window down. We pleasantly introduced ourselves & then I asked a few blunt & straight forward questions regarding to what he is/was transporting/delivering to the Wastewater Treatment Plant. His response was that he is cleaning out Septic Tanks in the township of Yankalilla & he has to bring the septic here. I replied by informing him of the issue that has just been caused by his delivery, & this treatment plant does not accept sand as it causes issues with the process & that this plant is not designed for such product. Informed this driver that no sand is to be delivered to this plant. Walked to receival station & gave a quick clean ready for next days work.

o	PC headed to switch room and isolated Blower#1 main circuit breaker to cut power from the area.

•	16:17 PC notified Operations Manager, who notified Regional Manager.
•	17:56 PC’s ensured site was safe but untouched, captured critical details and left site.

Location Description: Port Pirie Activated Sludge WWTP (Kitchener Tce)
Incident Detailed Description:
A sewer overflow was discovered by the Maintenance team (operator on leave) during a site visit to complete repairs at the Pirie Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP). It was determined that the plant's PLC had been switched off the day before at 15:45 and did not resume operation when powered back on. As a result, all communications from the plant were frozen from 15:45 on the 24th until the PLC was restarted at 10:35 on the 25th.
Aside from a minor overflow caused by blocked screens and high water levels in the "Online" basin, the plant was not significantly impacted, and it came back online without issue. Alarms were triggered by the PLC, but at the same time, a PLC alarm for Whyalla Water Reclamation Plant (WRP) also appeared. We later discovered that both alarms are connected to the same alert for unknown reasons.
Due to ongoing work on the alarm systems (SCADA team re-enabling some previously disabled alarm areas), we initially assumed the Whyalla alarm was related to this work. Upon investigating the Whyalla issue on the 24th, we found its PLC to be functioning correctly. Based on this, we assumed the alarm was linked to the system changes and deferred further investigation until the following morning.
This is why we missed the legitimate Pirie alarm
